summary: PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 is an unusually careful extraction. Its 154 items track the author version closely, all 38 cited library declarations (29 items) exist at the pins and say what the items claim, and the recorded source issues stand. Two findings survive. (1, medium) Route 7 makes AutomorphicCongruences:L4 the owner of the general theorem that a normal noetherian domain is the intersection of its height-one localizations, with two associated-prime lemmas. L4 is a late automorphic layer: in the production graph it has 846 ancestor stages across 120 roadmaps, KatoEulerSystems among them. Importing a basic commutative-algebra theorem from it makes the proposed definability Part II downstream of most of the automorphic atlas. The brief's 'early algebraic portion of L4' is not a stage, so the atlas cannot express it. §15 asks for the most foundational owner, and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 (5 ancestors, already planning associated-prime and dimension lemmas) is one. (2, low) The fundamental-equality item says the pin 'supplies only the separable function-field wrapper'. Tau Ceti also has the affine-model identity without any separability hypothesis, which leaves only finite normalization as the missing input. Route 3's reason also both assigns and does not assign that equality to A0-extension.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-442dc5, continuing Codex checkpoints (codex-a71f92, codex-c83e7a, codex-hjdg0j), and the review is REV-PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither.

Read arXiv 2012.01307v2 in full (19 pp., SHA-256 f9f26f7d…2c1f, matching the extraction; downloaded 2026-09-30) and kept v1 (SHA-256 93e6c612…b424) for comparison. Re-derived the hypothesis bookkeeping of Lemma 3.6 (d−2 parameters in characteristic 0, d−1 in characteristic p), Proposition 3.8 (Σ-unit choice against Lemma 3.5's v(a_1)>0 places), Proposition 3.2(3) (the dimension drop for any nontrivial valuation, and the C_{e+1} bound in characteristic p), the nonreal-place bound of E6, and Theorem 4.2(2) (the pole divisor via Tau Ceti's prescribed-pole theorem, which needs n ≥ 2g and exact constants).

Compared the statements of the 78 theorem items located at Theorems 1.1–1.3, Facts 2.1–2.3 and 3.1, Propositions 3.2, 3.4, 3.8, 3.10 and 5.1, Lemmas 3.5, 3.6, 3.9 and 5.3, and Theorem 4.2 with the paper. No hypothesis was dropped or strengthened: Fact 2.2's positive dimension, Proposition 3.4(2)'s parity for some 1 ≤ i ≤ d, Proposition 3.10's θ = (a_{d−1}⋯a_1)^N, and the empty-V_a case of Theorem 4.2(1).

Library claims: all 38 cited declarations (29 items) exist in the baseline index at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474. Read at the pinned commits: Place.exists_ord_eq_neg_and_forall_ne_ord_nonneg (HighDegree.lean:249: hF, hex, 2·genus ≤ n); isDiscreteValuationRing_of_isFunctionField (OfValuationSubring.lean:217); exists_forall_mem_valuation_sub_le_and_forall_mem_integers (StrongApproximation.lean:88: hS : S ≠ univ, s ⊆ S, hex); Place.exists_ne_zero_forall_mem_ord_eq (Approximation.lean:131). Each matches its item's statement and hypotheses.

Searched Tau Ceti for the fundamental equality. Found sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable (Place/Extension/Fundamental.lean:77, [Algebra.IsSeparable F F']), sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_le_finrank (Fibre.lean:300), and sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank (AffineModel/Extension.lean:293, no separability, Dedekind models R, S with Module.Finite R S). Tau Ceti has no general construction of finite Dedekind models in the inseparable case, so the item's 'planned' status stands.

Searched both libraries for the height-one intersection theorem. Mathlib has only the Dedekind case (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.iInf_localization_eq_bot, Ideal/Lemmas.lean:564) and the valuation-ring form Subring.eq_iInf_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn (Valuation/LocalSubring.lean:199). The general normal-noetherian statement is absent, so 'planned or missing' is right. The finding concerns its owner.

Routes: all seven route targets exist. The QuadraticFormInvariants document explicitly excludes 'the general theory of n-fold Pfister forms … Arason-Pfister … function-field methods', so route 5's Part II is not a re-plan. No stage plans Gabber's prime-to-ℓ alterations; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 plans de Jong's, so route 6 is sound. Route 4 coalesces into the pending DESIGN-LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheoryPartII. A0-extension plans 'finite normalization under excellence', matching route 3.

Owner depth on the production graph (scripts.build.assemble at the current revision): ancestor stages of AutomorphicCongruences:L4, 846 over 120 roadmaps; of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3, 5; of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension, 5; of LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0, 0; of LD.1, 1. Other consumers of the same theorem were found: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/bidual-intersection states A = ⋂ A_𝔭 as a hypothesis, and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/tate-generic-fibre-theorem uses it as a reduction step.

Source issues: re-read E1–E4, E6–E18 at their locators. My independent read of Lemma 5.3 (W_T used for rank-e flags) and of the ζ choice coincides with E3 and E4. The §10-style cross-references and the bibliography misprints agree. No source issue affects a stated result, so the absent sourceVersions field is not required by §18.

findings.claim: The general commutative-algebra theorem that a normal noetherian domain equals the intersection of its localizations at height-one primes, with its two associated-prime lemmas, is routed to AutomorphicCongruences:L4, a late automorphic layer. PROTOCOL §15 asks that a missing general notion be planned once, in the most general form, in the roadmap that owns it, usually the most foundational one. L4 is instead one of the deepest layers in the atlas. It requires AutomorphicCongruences:L3 and KatoEulerSystems:L4. The route 4 brief asks the Part II to import the theorem from 'the early algebraic portion' of L4, but no such stage exists, and the atlas links stages. As written, the proposed FinitelyGeneratedFieldDefinability Part II therefore inherits every prerequisite of L4. At least two other consumers (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1) need the same theorem. The review moved it away from A0-extension 'to avoid duplicate ownership', but the audit of L4 records what L4 needs; it is not an ownership decision.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 ('Give equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules. State hypotheses on catenarity and excellence …') and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension each have 5. The item note reads: 'Removed from the A0-extension route to avoid duplicate ownership.' Mathlib 082e2d3 has only the Dedekind case, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.iInf_localization_eq_bot (RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Lemmas.lean:564).
findings.fix: Re-route krull-intersection, principal-associated-height-one and associated-localization-detection to a foundational commutative-algebra owner. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 already plans associated-prime and dimension lemmas and has 5 ancestors. Keep the missing/planned statuses, and name R03.3 in the route 4 brief instead of AutomorphicCongruences:L4. findings.claim: The item's note says 'The pin supplies only the separable function-field wrapper; Mathlib supplies the finite-flat algebra identity.' That understates the pinned library. Tau Ceti f790474 also proves the fundamental identity at every place of a finite chart, for affine Dedekind models R ⊂ S with S finite over R, with no separability hypothesis. It is the separability-free statement Lemma 3.6 needs, provided a finite Dedekind model exists. The one missing input for the purely inseparable case is therefore finite normalization, which the extraction already plans. Separately, route 3's reason says the fundamental equality 'also belongs here' (A0-extension) and, in the next sentence, that it is 'imported, not assigned to this source route'.
